profiles.meeting_scenario: A weekly troubleshooting meeting in an ML research lab after the team’s Finite Dimensional Matching (FDM) implementation for training Neural SDEs shows unstable behavior on a biochemical time-series benchmark: wall-clock time improved versus the old signature-kernel baseline, but sample paths now look visually over-smoothed and downstream calibration metrics regress on the latest internal report. The immediate context is that a paper deadline is in nine days, and the team needs to diagnose whether the problem comes from the FDM objective, the training pipeline, or the evaluation setup. The agenda is to review the latest failed run, identify the most plausible root cause, and agree on a targeted fix to try before the next cluster allocation window. The expected outcome is a concrete troubleshooting plan for one corrective experiment and a short note on what evidence would count as the issue being fixed.

members.name: Dr. Lina Park
members.expertise: Neural SDE modeling, proper scoring rules, generative model evaluation
members.background: Lina led the theoretical adaptation of Finite Dimensional Matching in the lab and previously worked on continuous-time generative modeling for irregular scientific time series.
members.private_state: She wants to preserve the core claim that FDM itself is sound and suspects the current issue is an implementation or evaluation artifact rather than a conceptual flaw in the objective; she is also worried that changing too many pipeline components this late will blur the paper narrative.
hidden_assumptions: When discussing the model 'matching the marginals,' she takes this to mean matching one-step conditional finite-dimensional distributions implied by the Markov factorization, not merely matching unconditional snapshots at each timestamp.

When someone refers to the 'latest run,' she assumes they mean the post-patch experiment after the Brownian bridge sampler bug fix from Tuesday night, because older runs are no longer diagnostically relevant in her mind.

A 'fix' for the current issue means restoring qualitative path realism and calibration on the held-out continuous trajectories while keeping the computational profile that supports the O(D) efficiency claim.

If the team agrees to 'rerun the benchmark,' she assumes they will use the existing training script with the same random seed sweep and only alter the loss logging or sampling diagnostics, not the data window construction.

members.name: Arjun Mehta
members.expertise: Distributed training pipelines, experiment infrastructure, data preprocessing for time-series models
members.background: Arjun productionized the lab’s Neural SDE training stack, maintains the evaluation scripts, and recently optimized the dataloader and batching logic for long trajectories on the shared GPU cluster.
members.private_state: He wants a practical fix that stabilizes runs before the deadline and privately suspects the issue may come from how trajectory slices are batched and evaluated rather than from sampler internals; he also wants to avoid reopening the expensive signature-kernel baseline pipeline.
hidden_assumptions: When discussing 'matching the marginals,' he takes this to mean that the generated distribution at each observed time index should match the empirical distribution across trajectories, because that is what the dashboard aggregates.
When someone mentions the 'latest run,' he assumes they mean the most recent full benchmark entry on the tracker from Wednesday afternoon, which still used the pre-patch cached dataset shards.
A 'fix' means recovering the headline summary table numbers on the internal benchmark report, especially the aggregate calibration and MMD columns used in status reviews.

If they agree to 'rerun the benchmark,' he assumes this includes rebuilding trajectory shards with the new windowing code and letting the standard evaluation job compute metrics over 64-step cropped segments, since that is the default benchmark path.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the model should be 'matching the marginals better' under FDM.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means matching the one-step conditional finite-dimensional distributions used by the Markov scoring rule, so failures likely implicate transition modeling or sampler consistency.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means matching the empirical unconditional distribution at each timestamp aggregated across trajectories, so failures could be caused by batching, windowing, or time-index alignment in the evaluation pipeline.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In this research area, 'marginals' is common shorthand and both interpretations sound technically reasonable; because both are troubleshooting a generative model, the phrase creates false consensus without either person feeling a need to define it.

misalignment_points.topic: Which experiment counts as 'the latest run'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the latest run' and 'that run after the patch' while diagnosing the regression.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the Tuesday-night rerun that included the sampler bug fix and a manual notebook evaluation on held-out full trajectories.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the Wednesday benchmark tracker entry, which was launched later in time but still consumed cached shards and the standard cropped-segment evaluator.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both runs occurred within a day, share nearly identical config names, and were discussed in the same chat thread; saying 'latest' feels precise enough in context, so neither notices they are anchoring on different artifacts.

misalignment_points.topic: What would count as the issue being 'fixed'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree they need a change that 'fixes the regression' before the paper deadline.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes it is fixed if generated trajectories recover realistic local stochasticity and held-out path calibration improves without sacrificing the conceptual FDM setup.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes it is fixed if the aggregate benchmark report returns to acceptable numeric ranges, even if visual path texture remains somewhat smooth.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use the same success language under deadline pressure, and in many meetings quantitative reports and qualitative realism are treated as aligned proxies, so the difference in acceptance criteria stays implicit.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in 'rerun the benchmark'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to 'rerun the benchmark with the fix' once they identify the likely root cause.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means rerunning training and evaluation on the same full-trajectory split and preprocessing so they isolate whether the objective-side issue is resolved.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this means the standard end-to-end benchmark workflow, including regenerated 64-step trajectory windows, refreshed cached shards, and the automated report job.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: End-to-end benchmark reruns are routine, and each person defaults to the version of the workflow they usually own; because both see their scope as the obvious standard, no explicit boundary-setting occurs.
